intro: Eleven hundred metres down, the cable went slack and the radio went strange, and what came back up the line was not speech but a long, low tone that the divers learned to hear as music. Down in the bathysphere they keep a wall of cork, and each day, when the shift ends, the diver on watch pins up a scrap with the day's readings, written in a hand that has grown cramped from the cold. The old diver who mends the lamps has taken to pulling one pin from each scrap every evening, and the cork wall holds the rest, a forest of paper leaves, each missing exactly one small thing. He says the scraps are getting hard to read, not from the damp but from a habit of his own, and he has started a notebook of the pins, one page to a day, so that the missing pieces might be found again. Nobody asks him why.
echo: What drowns strong swimmers is never the wave you can see, but the pull going the other way beneath it.

meta.title: Meta: The Bathysphere Logs
meta.flavor: Nothing reached the bathysphere undamaged. The damage, though, was remarkably consistent.
